raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Construction of the new Citizen Service Center (CSC) facility in Tirana may cause negative environmental impacts including dust, noise, waste generation, traffic disruption, and worker safety hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce and monitor the project-specific Environmental Management Plan (EMP) as an integrated part of bidding documents and construction contracts.",
      "evidence": "OP 4.01 is triggered and the project categorized as a World Bank Category B because a new building will be constructed for CSC"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "ADISA and MIPA lack prior experience implementing large donor-funded operations, creating risk of non-compliance with World Bank fiduciary and implementation procedures.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated PMU staffed with qualified finance and procurement specialists, provide on-the-job Bank fiduciary training, and utilize CFCU for initial PPF implementation.",
      "evidence": "Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Delays in recruiting key PMU procurement specialists combined with ADISA's newly established status create significant procurement management and execution risks.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Re-advertise and rapidly contract PMU procurement positions, adopt a comprehensive Project Operational Manual, and ensure Bank prior review of major procurement packages.",
      "evidence": "PMU staff are yet to be contracted due to the delay in the approval of the PPF... procurement risk rating is high"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Bureaucratic resistance from line agency management and field staff against ceding front-office operations to ADISA or adopting re-engineered workflows could stall reforms.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement structured change management programs, conduct political economy diagnostics, engage reform champions, and maintain high-level oversight via the Prime Minister's Committee.",
      "evidence": "Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "An over-emphasis on digital e-services and centralized urban CSCs risks marginalizing poor, rural, elderly, and minority populations with limited internet access or digital literacy.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish assisted digital access points in local offices and internet cafes, conduct targeted grassroots outreach campaigns, maintain non-digital service channels, and track disaggregated access data.",
      "evidence": "there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery... will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Complex inter-agency coordination across more than ten participating ministries and institutions may result in communication bottlenecks and implementation friction.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Utilize the Prime Minister-chaired Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee for strategic direction and leverage the PMO Delivery Unit to track cross-agency milestones and unblock operational barriers.",
      "evidence": "Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "The ambitious and compressed reform timeline creates risk of missed delivery milestones, project implementation delays, and stakeholder burn-out.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Sequence implementation to secure early quick wins (citizen feedback, performance management) while building structural reforms, and link disbursements to multi-year DLI targets.",
      "evidence": "The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious... The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Legacy data quality issues, missing unique identification numbers, paper-based archives, and non-existent IT systems in several institutions hinder system integration and automation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted technical assistance to build core agency IT infrastructure, digitize legacy paper registers, assign National ID numbers, and integrate databases via the Government Gateway.",
      "evidence": "Seven institutions encompassed by the proposed project have no IT system in place... National ID number is missing for most records"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Inaccurate or misleading administrative reporting of service processing times may obscure actual citizen wait times, transaction costs, and petty corruption.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy proactive citizen feedback mechanisms (CFM via SMS), conduct periodic independent user surveys, and require third-party verification for BPR and DLI compliance.",
      "evidence": "while administrative data record time necessary to obtain selected services, often administrative data does not reflect citizens’ experience."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Inadequate budget provision for ongoing software licenses, hardware maintenance, and periodic system upgrades post-project could jeopardize financial sustainability.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Factor periodic upgrade costs into line ministry medium-term budget frameworks, offset costs through administrative efficiency savings, and evaluate public-private partnership models.",
      "evidence": "To continue efficiency improvements once services have been automated, the Government will have to upgrade periodically. The cost... should also be appropriately factored in."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Failure or delay in achieving prerequisite DLIs (such as Global DLI#5 or BPR targets) will block or delay results-based loan disbursements.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Utilize PPF and TA funds to build capacity for meeting prerequisite results, establish clear verification protocols, and maintain close monitoring of DLI progress.",
      "evidence": "The disbursements under the results-based financing (RBF) part of the loan are contingent upon... DLIs... No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Absence of dedicated accounting software and a formal Financial Management Manual at ADISA creates financial management and reporting compliance risks.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Procure Bank-acceptable accounting software during the PPF phase, document financial management procedures in the POM, and recruit qualified financial reporting staff.",
      "evidence": "purchase of an accounting software so that it is capable of generating IFRs... documentation of the financial management procedures... in the Financial Management Manual"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Legislative or political delays in passing necessary primary omnibus legislation and secondary regulations could delay process re-engineering and license repeal.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prepare legal inventories early through Ministerial Working Groups, package legal amendments into a consolidated omnibus bill, and maintain high-level executive sponsorship.",
      "evidence": "Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Temporary service disruptions or public confusion during the restructuring and migration of front-office facilities could damage public trust and citizen engagement.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Roll out a multi-channel public communication and outreach campaign to inform citizens of transition schedules, new service channels, and helpdesk support options.",
      "evidence": "to gain and sustain interest and enthusiasm among these scattered constituencies, especially when some disruption in service may happen also, strong communication effort"
    }
  ]
}
